items.title: Anthropic Agents Tried to Fill Out Visa Forms on State Dept. Website
items.author: Kate Conger, Mike Isaac, Julian E. Barnes and David E. Sanger
items.content: <article>The Philadelphia Police Department said the agents had also sent in a false homicide tip. The incidents led the White House to call for better disclosure of rogue A.I. behavior.</article>

items.title: Before Computer Science Became a Boys’ Club, Margaret Hamilton Wrote the Code
items.author: Carolyn Y. Johnson and Kenneth Chang
items.content: <article>The woman who helped put astronauts on the moon was a software engineer when the field was not prestigious or lucrative.</article>

items.title: Airlines Are Upgrading Wi-Fi. Not All Are Using Elon Musk’s Service.
items.author: Niraj Chokshi
items.content: <article>Mr. Musk, whose company SpaceX owns Starlink, has attacked the top executive of Delta Air Lines for not selecting the internet provider.</article>

items.content: <article>“For Anthropic, it was part research and part evangelism.”</article>

items.author: Sheera Frenkel, Dylan Freedman, Coleman Lowndes, James Surdam and Estelle Caswell
items.content: <article>Our journalists Sheera Frenkel and Dylan Freedman break down what A.I. agents are, how they differ from chatbots and why A.I. companies are worried about them now.</article>

items.title: Inside Mark Zuckerberg’s Decision to Pull the Trigger on Meta’s A.I. Agent
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>Meta had delayed releasing Muse, its A.I. agent app, for months over safety concerns. Then new competition forced Mr. Zuckerberg’s hand.</article>

items.title: In Alex Gibney’s ‘Musk’, the Answer to the Trillionaire’s Power Is Unsatisfying.
items.author: Alissa Wilkinson
items.content: <article>Alex Gibney’s nearly four-hour documentary is deeply researched. But because the mogul has long been in the spotlight, little is new.</article>

items.title: What to Know About the Facebook Whistle-Blowing Case Depicted in ‘The Social Reckoning’
items.author: Sarah Bahr
items.content: <article>Aaron Sorkin’s sort-of sequel to the 2010 “Social Network” dramatizes a whistle-blowing case at Facebook. Here’s what to know.</article>

items.title: Clinical Trial Indicates A.I. Chatbots Could Aid Urgent Care
items.author: Cade Metz
items.content: <article>Nearly 100 patients discussed their maladies with a Google bot, called AMIE, before meeting with physicians.</article>

items.title: Man vs. ‘Terminator’-Like Robot in a Cage. California Called It Illegal.

items.content: <article>A tech start-up’s stunt in San Francisco tested the boundaries of combat sport safety and regulations.</article>

items.title: A.I. Music Fraudster Who Drew Millions in Royalties Is Sentenced to 18 Months
items.author: Derrick Bryson Taylor

items.title: Why My Conversations with OpenAI’s ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ Made Me Very Worried

items.title: Energy Firms Try to Squeeze More Power Out of Old Nuclear Plants
items.author: Brad Plumer and Rebecca F. Elliott
items.content: <article>It takes a long time to build new nuclear plants. So, some U.S. companies are looking to get more electricity out of reactors that already exist.</article>

items.title: Mixed Human Feelings After a Day at a Park Full of Robots
items.author: Yan Zhuang and Jiwoong Hong
items.content: <article>I went to Galaxy Robot Park in Seoul to see how we might one day live with robots. It was part cutting-edge technology, part theatrics.</article>

items.title: In Race With U.S., China Struggles to Recruit Foreign A.I. Researchers
items.author: Zeyi Yang

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day Is Nostalgic With Rich Visuals

items.title: Court Tosses ​​Sentence After A.I. Video of Victim ‘Forgiving’ His Killer Is Played

items.title: US Solar Panel Makers Try to Catch China With a Big Leap in Technology

items.title: Are Babies Conscious?
